title: Skimming & scanning
examples: When should I use skimming versus scanning?
Is there a best way to speed up my reading?
What is the difference between finding the main idea and finding a specific fact?

explain.say: Today we are learning two useful reading skills. These skills help you read faster and smarter. We will learn about skimming and scanning today.
Skimming means reading quickly to get the main idea. You look over the text to understand the general topic. Think of it like getting the overall picture first.

items: Step 2: Read first and last sentences

explain.say: Scanning means looking quickly for one specific piece of information. You are hunting for a particular fact or name. You do not read everything in between.

items: Step 1: Know what you are looking for
Step 2: Move your eyes across the text
Step 3: Stop when you find the fact

explain.say: For example, if you are reading about world capitals, skimming gives you the general idea. Scanning helps you find only the capital of France.
In real life, imagine you are looking through old phone books. You are scanning for your mum's name. You do not read every single name.
A common mistake is trying to read every word slowly. This makes you miss the overall point. Remember to first skim for the topic.

items: Skim first for the main idea
Then scan for the detail needed

faq.q: How long should I spend skimming a chapter?
faq.a: You should spend just a very short time skimming. Aim to read only the introduction and conclusion first. You can also look at the headings and subheadings.
asks: How fast should I read to get the gist?
Is there a time limit for skimming?

faq.q: Can I use skimming and scanning at the same time?
faq.a: You should use them in order, not at the same time. First, skim to understand the general idea. Then, scan when you need a specific fact. This gives you the best result.
asks: Do I do both techniques together?
What is the order for these skills?

faq.q: What if I don't know what I am looking for?
faq.a: If you do not know what you are looking for, you should skim first. This will help you understand the context. Once you know the context, you can scan better.
asks: Should I skim if I don't know the answer?
How does knowing the topic help my scanning?

faq.q: Is skimming good for understanding the details?
faq.a: No, skimming is not good for details. It gives you the big picture only. You must scan or read carefully for the small facts.
asks: Can I learn details just by skimming?

faq.q: Does my reading speed change when I practice these skills?
faq.a: Yes, practicing these techniques will help your speed. You will start to see the main ideas and facts much faster. Keep practicing with different texts.
asks: Will I get faster by doing this?
How long does it take to get better at this?

facts: Skimming is for understanding the general idea or main concept.
Scanning is for locating a specific piece of information, like a date or name.
It is best to skim first, and then scan if needed.
These techniques help you read much faster than reading every word.

quiz.say: A student needs to find the year the Great Wall was built.
quiz.why: You skim to get the general idea of the article. Then you scan specifically for dates or numbers.

wrong.1: This is too slow and will make you miss the specific date you are looking for.
wrong.2: The specific date might be in the middle or the last paragraph.
wrong.3: Headings give the topic, but they do not contain the exact date you need.

quiz.say: You are reading a science report and need to know the chemical formula for water.

options.show: Guess the answer from the title.
options.say: Guess the answer from the title.

quiz.why: Skimming gives you the context of science. Scanning allows you to quickly spot the formula H2O.

wrong.0: Diagrams show the concept, but the formula is written in the text.
wrong.1: The title only tells you the subject, not the exact formula.
wrong.3: Reading slowly wastes time when you only need one formula.

quiz.say: A teacher asks you to summarize a chapter about Roman history quickly.

options.show: Look only at the first page.
options.say: Look only at the first page.

quiz.why: To summarize, you need the main ideas, which is what skimming does best.

wrong.0: This is too time-consuming for a quick summary.
wrong.1: The main ideas are spread throughout the entire chapter.
wrong.3: Scanning only finds names; it does not help you summarize the whole chapter.
